newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end lower with U.S., pare some losses.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end lower with U.S., pare some losses.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed lower on Wednesday amid weakness in U.S. Treasuries and some foreign selling, but strengthened from lows earlier in the session, dealers said.
"Today I think it was just in sympathy with the U.S.," said Dan Kelly, director of financial markets research with CIBC Wood Gundy Securities. "The economic landscape really has not changed."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$1.10 to C$110.55 to yield 7.109 percent. The U.S. 30-year bonds fell 1-24/32 to yield 6.62 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 50 basis points from 51 basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday. The spread widened to as much as 56 basis points earlier in the session.
Canadian bonds tumbled with U.S. Treasuries this morning amid technical selling and concern that Japanese financial institutions might reduce their purchases of North American bonds.
Canadian issues underperformed U.S. bonds initally as some foreign bondholders sold in order to lock in healthy profits made on Canadian bonds this year.
But Canada's positive bond market fundamentals, as well as a firmer dollar, helped the market to pare some losses by the end of the session, analyts said.

"It's technical traders that are controlling the market right now and everyone's got sell signals. Basically everyone is looking for an excuse to sell," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn Capital Inc. "The fundamentals haven't really changed."
CIBC Wood Gundy's Kelly said that Canadian bonds represented "a short-term buying opportunity," given the degree of the selloff.
In other prices, the Government of Canada 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.80 to C$103.70 to yield 6.489 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 1-5/32 to yield 6.38 percent.
The spread between the bonds narrowed to 11 basis points from 12 basis points at Tuesday's close. The spread widened as much as 21 basis points earlier in the session.
Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 3.01 percent against the U.S. bill at 4.97 percent.
